'''Carin Bondar''' (born 20 May 1975) is a Canadian [[biologist]], writer, filmmaker, speaker and television personality. She is a host of ''[[Outrageous Acts of Science]]'', ''Stephen Hawking's Brave New World'', and ''Worlds Oddest Animal Couples''.<ref name="nsb">{{cite news|title=Dr. Carin Bondar – Biologist & Television Personality|url=https://www.nsb.com/speakers/carin-bondar/|access-date=1 December 2017|work=[[National Speakers Bureau]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=PsiVid – A cross section of science on the cyberscreen|url=https://blogs.scientificamerican.com/psi-vid/about/|access-date=1 December 2017|work=[[Scientific American]]|archive-date=7 July 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170707131301/https://blogs.scientificamerican.com/psi-vid/about/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Bondar was born in [[New Westminster]] and grew up near [[Vancouver]], [[British Columbia]]. She comes from a small family of [[French Canadians|French-Canadian]], Russian and [[British ancestry]]. She met mathematician Ian Affleck in 1995, became engaged in 1999 and married in 2001.<ref>{{cite news|title=Science Channel to Premiere New Season of OUTRAGEOUS ACTS OF SCIENCE, Today|url=https://www.broadwayworld.com/bwwtv/article/Science-Channel-to-Premiere-New-Season-of-OUTRAGEOUS-ACTS-OF-SCIENCE-1026-20161025|access-date=1 December 2017}}</ref>

After receiving a BSc from [[Simon Fraser University]] in 1999, she completed an MSc in evolution and development at the [[University of Victoria]] in 2001 and a PhD in freshwater population ecology from the [[University of British Columbia]].<ref name="tilleys"/> Bondar was forced to put her PhD studies on hold in 2005 while she took over a family business after the deaths of her father John Paul and her brother William Paul. She re-enrolled after a year's leave and completed her PhD in 2007.<ref name="sfu">{{cite news|title=Carin Bondar – Simon Fraser University|url=https://www.sfu.ca/science/alumni-community/inspiring-alumni1/profiles/carin-bondar.html|access-date=1 December 2017|work=[[Simon Fraser University]]|archive-date=9 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200809183754/http://www.sfu.ca/science/alumni-community/inspiring-alumni1/profiles/carin-bondar.html|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="ufv">{{cite news|last1=Russell|first1=Anne|title=Carin Bondar to speak on The Nature of Sex on Nov 26 at UFV|url=http://blogs.ufv.ca/blog/2015/11/dr-carin-bonda-nov-26-at-ufv/|access-date=1 December 2017|work=[[University of the Fraser Valley]]}}</ref>

==Career==
Bondar began a career in science communication while raising her four young children in [[Chilliwack]], British Columbia. Her first book, ''The Nature of Human Nature'' and her own personal biology blog led her to a blogging position with [[Scientific American]] in 2011.<ref name="Bondar2010">{{cite book |last= Bondar|first= Carin|title=The Nature of Human Nature |date= November 2010|isbn=9780557457939}}</ref> She was invited to appear in the [[Science Channel]]'s ''[[Outrageous Acts of Science]]'' in its first season, and she has maintained a hosting position on this TV show for all of its 6 seasons.<ref name="ufv"/>

Bondar has since written two more books and written/hosted several web and television programs on major networks. She has worked with The [[Science Channel]], [[Discovery Channel]], [[Animal Planet]], [[Netflix]]<ref name="Netflix">{{cite news|title=World's Oddest Animal Couples US|url=https://www.netflix.com/in/title/80106367|access-date=1 December 2017|work=[[Netflix]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1= HAUCK |first1=JENNA |title=Chilliwack biologist hosts TV show, releases book|url=http://www.theprogress.com/community/chilliwack-biologist-hosts-tv-show-releases-book/|access-date=1 December 2017|work=Chilliwack Progress|date=31 August 2016}}</ref> and [[National Geographic Wild]]. Her independent web series ''Wild Sex''<ref name="ideas.ted">{{cite news|title=The sexual deception of plants|url=https://ideas.ted.com/the-sexual-deception-of-plants/|access-date=1 December 2017|work=[[TED (conference)]]}}</ref> (produced by [[Earth-Touch|Earth Touch]], a [[South Africa]]n based natural history film production company), has engaged over 60 million viewers.<ref name="sfu"/> She presented on this topic at [[TED Global]] in Edinburgh, [[Scotland]] in 2013 – "The Birds and the Bees are just the Beginning".<ref>{{cite news|title=Carin Bondar – Wild sex biologist|url=https://www.ted.com/speakers/carin_bondar|access-date=1 December 2017|work=[[TED (conference)]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Meet the Outrageous Acts of Science Experts; Science Channel|url=http://www.sciencechannel.com/tv-shows/outrageous-acts-of-science/meet-the-outrageous-acts-of-science-experts/|access-date=1 December 2017|work=[[Science (TV network)]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Carin Bondar: Seks v svetu narave|url=http://www.mladina.si/181388/carin-bondar-seks-v-svetu-narave/|work=[[Mladina]]|language=sl|access-date=1 December 2017}}</ref>

Bondar is currently{{when|date=June 2019}} a writer and host of ''Wild Sex'',<ref name="ideas.ted"/> an animated series based on her book of the same title. She also wrote a book called ''Wild Moms'', published in 2018.<ref>{{cite news|title=Kirkus Wild Moms review|url=https://www.kirkusreviews.com/book-reviews/carin-bondar/wild-moms/|access-date=28 August 2022}}</ref> Bondar holds an adjunct professorship in the department of biology at the [[University of the Fraser Valley]] in [[British Columbia]],<ref name="tilleys">{{cite news|title=Dr Carin Bondar|url=http://www.tilleys.com.au/concerts/artist/dr-carin-bondar/|access-date=1 December 2017|work=Tilley's|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180312211650/http://tilleys.com.au/concerts/artist/dr-carin-bondar/|archive-date=12 March 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> and works with Taxon Expeditions, a [[Netherlands]]-based company that engages citizen scientists on scientific expeditions to discover new species. The group mainly works in the Sabah region of Borneo and has discovered seven new species.

Bondar is known for her bold approach to science storytelling. She has received accolades and global media-coverage for her music video parodies including a play on [[Miley Cyrus]]' "[[Wrecking Ball (Miley Cyrus song)|Wrecking Ball]]."<ref>{{cite news|last1=Wilcox|first1=Christie|title=Move over Miley: Dr. Bondar's 'Wrecking Ball' spoof is VMA-worthy!|url=http://blogs.discovermagazine.com/science-sushi/2014/01/12/move-miley-dr-bondars-wrecking-ball-spoof-vma-worthy/|access-date=1 December 2017|work=[[Discover (magazine)|Discover]]|date=12 January 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201182314/http://blogs.discovermagazine.com/science-sushi/2014/01/12/move-miley-dr-bondars-wrecking-ball-spoof-vma-worthy/|archive-date=1 December 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> She has appeared in several live events including I F*#cking Love Science Live,<ref>{{cite news|title=I F*#cking Love Science Live: Celebrating Science on a Whole New Level|url=https://blogs.scientificamerican.com/psi-vid/i-fcking-love-science-live-celebrating-science-on-a-whole-new-level/|access-date=1 December 2017|work=[[Scientific American]]|date=11 October 2013}}</ref> the Australian [[National Science Week]], and the [[Bay Area Science Festival]].

Bondar was elected to the Board of Education for the [[Chilliwack]] [[School District 33 Chilliwack|School District]] in 2022.<ref>https://www.chilliwack.com/main/page.cfm?id=2951</ref>
